subject: conceptual question: truncation without closed form

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: conceptual question: truncation without closed form
parts:
Hi,

Suppose I have

- (real) parameters a[N],b[N],m,
- a (known) function f,

and my data generating process is truncated, ie only observations with

f(a[i], b[i]) <= m

are kept in the data. Futhermore, there is no closed form for the
integral

Probability(f(a[i], b[i]) <= m | ...)

so I can't just include it in the likelihood function.

Is there any solution to this in Stan, eg some parameter augmentation or
transformation? Or what is the "standard" way of dealing with these
situations?

As a fallback, I can work out a good approximation to the integral (eg
Pade) and code it in Stan, but if possible I would not mind avoiding
that.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] conceptual question: truncation without closed form
parts:
We don't have any way (yet, at least) to define implicit functions;
it's part of our current NSF proposal, though, so maybe in a couple
of years :-)

So you're right that you need an approximation to the log CDF (left truncated)
or log CCDF (right truncated), or both (left and right truncated).

- Bob
